summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, COPD, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for worsening right leg cellulitis. Evaluation ruled out DVT but revealed signs concerning for osteomyelitis, leading to a PICC line placement for long-term IV antibiotics. She was also treated for a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli and managed for delirium, anemia, and a chronic leg ulcer. Her condition stabilized over nine days, with improvement in infection and mental status. She was discharged on home IV antibiotics with nursing support, follow-up arranged with multiple specialists, and education on wound care, diabetes management, and CPAP compliance.
